correctness.rationale: The three-step products are strictly positive, have common determinant −b³Q, and direct multiplication yields trace F+bL₋ for 123 and F+bL₊ for 132. Cyclic trace invariance gives all six orders. The positive root of z²−(F+bL)z−b³Q increases strictly with the trace; the oriented three-point determinant in 123 order equals −Δ. At z=1, since the other characteristic root is negative, the sign test is exactly R>1 iff F+bL+b³Q>1. These strictly increasing cubics start at F, determining two distinct positive crossings exactly when F<1 and Δ≠0; each equality is neutral for the linear dynamics. A positive left Perron vector ensures a nonzero leading coefficient for every nonnegative nonzero start, and the two other phases inherit the growth factor. For two seasons AB and BA have the same trace and determinant; the stated three-season witness shows sharpness. An independent exact replay verifies both witness signs over all six permutations and brackets both reported crossing values by rational evaluations.
residual_risks: Deterministic two-stage linear system only; the result does not give stochastic extinction or nonlinear abundance. The uploaded ordering test uses floating square roots and does not replace the exact trace proof.

originality.rationale: The signed-area ranking, tie and threshold law are mathematically covered by a stronger distinct indexed result, f3fd50e75a7e, whose linear-product subsystem is decisive even though its main model is nonlinear. Swapping coordinates conjugates each A_i to P_i=[[0,s_i],[b,f_i]]. Substituting (f'_i,s'_i,t'_i)=(s_i,b,f_i) into that record's exact calendar identities gives T₁₂₃−T₁₃₂=b det(f,s,1)=−bΔ and K=b³Q, with the same individual traces. Its proof consists of unrestricted polynomial identities, so the numerical constraints in its nonlinear theorem do not restrict this linear specialization. Its T+K test gives the very two cubics in the frozen claim; monotonicity and the open window follow immediately. This is demonstrable coverage, not a historical-priority claim: the stronger record has a later catalogue path. The published sources inspected establish general chronology effects and periodic projection background, not an early exact statement of these formulas.
